ev.q: Ratio of proportions (RPs) with 95% CIs were calculated to compare ED visits by incarcerated and nonincarcerated adults.
The nonincarcerated sample was used as the referent group for this analysis.
The proportion of visits due to assault and self-harm was about five times as high among incarcerated adults
CDC analyzed 2010–2019 National Electronic Injury Surveillance System–All Injury Program (NEISS-AIP) data.
NEISS-AIP collects data on patients treated in EDs for nonfatal injuries from a nationally representative, stratified probability sample of hospitals.

methods_quotes.q: Data are weighted by the inverse probability of selection to provide annual national estimates.
Ratio of proportions (RPs) with 95% CIs were calculated to compare ED visits by incarcerated and nonincarcerated adults.
Rao-Scott chi-square tests were used to calculate p-values, and p-values <0.05 were considered statistically significant.
SUDAAN Rlogist procedure was used to estimate RPs with 95% CIs by sex and age group among incarcerated adults.
Dashes indicate that values were suppressed because of either small sample size (<20 cases) or a weighted estimate <1,200.
